title: Org Join Governor: domain health scoring, team-level invite throttles, and audit-export
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem: Our current org/team onboarding controls are binary (allow/deny) and lack gradual enforcement and observability. This causes two pain points: (1) Fraudulent or low-quality domains bypass org vetting when attackers use transient domains, and (2) a lack of per-team throttles results in blast-radius for token leaks or automated signups.

Proposal: Implement an "Org Join Governor" service that combines: (A) a domain health scoring pipeline (reputation, MX/SPF/DMARC checks, historical invite accept rates), (B) configurable team-level invite throttles and burst policies, and (C) an audit-export endpoint for downstream SIEM and compliance ingestion. The Governor will surface decisions to the Console (per-org policy view) and emit structured audit events to our existing logging pipeline for RBAC v2 changes and invite lifecycle events.

Goals: Reduce unexpected org joins from suspicious domains by 80% in first month; allow enterprise admins to set per-team invite rate limits and automatic cooling; provide 90-day exportable audit trails for invite and domain-verification actions that include policy context and decision rationale.
acceptance_criteria: Domain health score calculated for every invite attempt and stored on invite record (0-100).
Per-team invite throttle config UI + API exposure; backend enforces burst and sustained limits.
Audit-export endpoint (S3/HTTP sink) emits NDJSON lines with schema: timestamp, org_id, actor_id, action, invite_id, domain_score, policy_version, decision_reason.
RBAC v2 mapping: decisions include which RBAC rule triggered (e.g., domain_allowlist/denylist, team-rate-limit) and link to policy id.
Migration script to backfill domain scores for invite history (last 90 days) for compliance exports.
Integration tests cover policy changes, throttling edge cases, and audit-event fidelity; performance tests show <15ms median added latency for invite path under normal load.
implementation_notes: Service: 'org-join-governor' as a small stateless microservice in Go behind the router; expose EvaluateInvite(org, invite_email, team) -> Decision + metadata.

Domain scoring: combine DNS checks (SPF/DMARC), MX existence, disposable-domain list match, historical accept-rate (from invite_events table) using a lightweight weights model stored in config and hot-reloadable.
Throttle store: Redis token-bucket per team with burst and refill parameters; fallback to global limits if Redis unavailable.
Audit export: write to kinesis -> processing lambda that normalizes and writes NDJSON to s3://redwood-audit-exports/{org}/{year}/{month}/, also optional webhook sink for enterprise customers.
RBAC v2 integration: Decision returns policy_hit string matching RBAC engine rule ids; add mapping table 'policy_versions' in pg to track changes for historical export.
UI/Console: new policy editor panel under Org Settings -> Security -> "Join Governor" with human-readable rule list and toggle to enable/disable automated cooling.
Performance: keep evaluation path synchronous and bounded; cache recent domain scores in in-memory LRU with TTL 15m to avoid repeated DNS work.
Data retention: invite decision records retained 1 year by default; export tool supports custom retention for enterprise (legal hold).

qa_steps: 1) Create test org and enable Join Governor policy with strict deny for disposable domains.
2) Attempt invites from disposable domains and verify immediate reject + audit event recorded.
3) Exercise team-level throttle: send 200 invites in 10s and confirm throttle triggers and uses burst policy; verify token-bucket metrics in Redis.
4) Run export job for last 7 days and validate NDJSON schema and included decision_reason fields.
5) Load test invite path with 1k rps synthetic traffic; measure added p50/p95 latency attributed to Governor service in tracing.
6) Simulate Redis outage and confirm fallback to global limit with an appropriate audit note.
